questions.prompt: Put the parts of a short project demo in order.
items: Say what problem the project solves
Run it and show the core features working
Explain briefly how it works inside
Say what you learned and what you would do next
questions.explain: The problem comes first because it is what makes the rest worth watching. Code shown before anyone knows what it is for is just code.

questions.prompt: You have five minutes. What should the demo actually show?
choices: The core features doing a real job, start to finish
The parts you found hardest to write
questions.explain: A demo is evidence that the thing works. Watching it do one real job is stronger evidence than a tour of everything it can do.

questions.prompt: Which of these are worth including when you present a project?
choices: Something that was hard, and how you got past it
An apology for the features you did not finish
questions.explain: The difficulty is often the most interesting part, because it is where the work went. Apologising spends your time on the version you did not build.

questions.prompt: Your program crashes during the live demo. What is the best response?
choices: Say what input caused it and what you think is wrong, then carry on with the rest
Move on quickly and hope nobody saw
Restart and try exactly the same input again
questions.explain: Diagnosing a crash out loud is itself a demonstration of skill. Hiding it is the only version of this that costs you anything.
